initial_pdf_review.contribution: For every n, the four images of the single fixed Fox row generate the integral group rings of A8 x C2 and A8 as two-sided ideals under the displayed maps. This rules out annihilating the row in every nonzero ring image through either map. The p-group lift corollary extends this conclusion to the indicated finite quotients over commutative coefficient rings in which p is nilpotent.
conceptual_argument: The braid crossing rules conserve the ordered product, so three closure relators suffice. The terminal twists affect slots 1 and 2 only. This fixes R0 and its four evaluated Fox derivatives across the family.

At each sign of the central involution, sum conjugates of a two-sided-ideal element over a subgroup H. On an H-orbit O each output coefficient is its input orbit total times |H|/|O|. The full A8 average then produces 20160 times the identity from the claimed integral orbit totals. For p = 3, 5, 7, the relevant subgroup order is prime to p and the claimed modular orbit totals give an invertible scalar. The two signs coincide modulo 2 and use the cited convolution.

For a sign ideal J, the additive quotient B/J is killed by 20160. The reductions imply that multiplication by each prime divisor of 20160 is surjective on B/J. Multiplication by 20160 is therefore both zero and surjective, yielding B/J = 0.

Each sign evaluation lifts 1 to an element of the original ideal. The differences from 1 lie in (z - 1) and (z + 1), whose product is zero. This gives 1 in the original ideal over the integers, including the prime 2, by expanding the product of the differences.

For a finite normal p-group kernel, the augmentation ideal of its group algebra in characteristic p is nilpotent by central order-p induction. Normality extends nilpotence to the kernel of the quotient group algebra map. A lift of 1 from the row ideal is a unit. Lifting twice, first modulo pR and then across the nilpotent ideal pR[Q], handles nilpotent p in R.
